chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla from al-Washa from Aban ibn Uthman from Ismail al-Ju'fi who said:
I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Al-Mughira ibn Sa'id reported from you that you said to him, 'The menstruating woman makes up the prayer.'

So he (peace be upon him) said, 'What is the matter with him? May Allah not reconcile him. The wife of Imran vowed what was in her belly as a dedicated one, and the dedicated one for the Masjid enters it, then does not come out of it ever.'
So when she gave birth to it, she said, 'My Lord, surely I have brought it forth a female – (and Allah was more Knowing of what she gave birth to) - and the male is not like the female.'
So when she had given birth to her, she entered her into the Masjid. So the Prophets drew lots over her, and the vote came out for Zakariyya, and Zakariyya took the responsibility for her.
Thus, she did not come out from the Masjid until she was an adult. So when she became an adult to what the women tend to reach in adulthood, she went out.
So was she able upon making up for those days which she went out, and it was upon her that she would happen to be in the Masjid for ever?
ai.seo_question: Does a menstruating woman need to make up her missed prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) refutes Al-Mughira ibn Sa'id's report that a menstruating woman makes up her missed prayers (salat) by employing an analogical argument from the life of Maryam (peace be upon her). He cites the precedent of Maryam, who was dedicated to the Masjid and remained there permanently, to argue that if she did not make up the days she left the Masjid to give birth, then a menstruating woman certainly does not make up her missed prayers.
